top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) is the best-confirmed and best-attributed candidate: magic-wavelength trapping is independently reproduced at the 1e-18 level by several laboratories, calculable atomic theory controls the main systematics, and it already yields physics (millimetre-scale redshift, bounds on drifting constants, many-body regime). The two-name allocation is clean and the citation can be scoped to the lattice scheme, distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes. IceCube is a genuine discovery but ranks second because the three-name allocation is contested and source identification is still immature; a mature prize this year is preferable to no award.
